For each integer \(n\ge2\), let \(\mathcal K_n\) consist of all sets \(K=\overline\Omega\subset\mathbb C^n\), where \(\Omega\) is a nonempty bounded connected open set with \(C^\infty\) boundary.

Use the following orientation convention for pseudoconvexity. Near each \(q\in\partial K\), take a smooth real defining function \(\rho\) with \(K\cap U=\{\rho\le0\}\) and \(d\rho\ne0\) on \(\partial K\cap U\). The boundary \(\partial K\) is pseudoconvex if, at every such \(q\),
\[
\sum_{j,k=1}^{n}\rho_{z_j\bar z_k}(q)v_j\overline{v_k}\ge0
\qquad\text{whenever}\qquad
\sum_{j=1}^{n}\rho_{z_j}(q)v_j=0.
\]

An open set \(Y\subset\mathbb C^n\) is called Oka if, for every integer \(m\ge1\), every nonempty compact convex set \(Q\subset\mathbb C^m\), every holomorphic map \(f:V\to Y\) on an open neighbourhood \(V\) of \(Q\), and every \(\varepsilon>0\), there is a holomorphic map \(F:\mathbb C^m\to Y\) satisfying
\[
\sup_{x\in Q}\|F(x)-f(x)\|<\varepsilon,
\]
where the norm is Euclidean.

Define the two sets of dimensions
\[
\begin{aligned}
S&=\bigl\{n\in\mathbb Z_{\ge2}:\ \text{for every }K\in\mathcal K_n,\quad
\partial K\text{ pseudoconvex}\ \Longrightarrow\ \mathbb C^n\setminus K\text{ Oka}\bigr\},\\
N&=\bigl\{n\in\mathbb Z_{\ge2}:\ \text{for every }K\in\mathcal K_n,\quad
\mathbb C^n\setminus K\text{ Oka}\ \Longrightarrow\ \partial K\text{ pseudoconvex}\bigr\}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Determine exactly the ordered pair \((S,N)\).

I’m unable to supply the complete proof requested. In particular, I cannot reliably identify and justify the recent result needed to determine both dimension sets, and I should not substitute a guessed pair or a theorem I cannot verify.

One necessary implication can be established: \(2\in N\). If \(\partial K\subset\mathbb C^2\) is not pseudoconvex, its Levi form is negative at some point. With the exterior orientation, that point is strictly pseudoconvex for \(Y=\mathbb C^2\setminus K\). A local holomorphic peak function there, patched with a constant using a maximum, gives a bounded, continuous, nonconstant plurisubharmonic function on \(Y\).

Such a function cannot exist on an Oka domain under the approximation definition in the question. Indeed, approximate the inclusion of any small closed ball \(Q\Subset Y\) by entire maps \(F_j:\mathbb C^2\to Y\). Each bounded plurisubharmonic function \(u\circ F_j\) is constant by Liouville’s theorem. Uniform convergence on \(Q\), together with continuity of \(u\), then forces \(u|_Q\) to be constant, contradicting the constructed function.

Thus **what is established here is \(2\in N\)**. The determination of \(S\) and the remaining dimensions in \(N\) is not established here; this is not a complete solution to your problem.
